estimator: Equal source mean of per-arm complete seed mean; paired difference of these source means. RFEDIT uses its single deterministic result, never duplicated.
bootstrap: 10000 source-resampling percentile 95% intervals, pointwise, not multiplicity-adjusted
p_test: two-sided source sign flip, 10000 Monte Carlo replicates, plus-one correction; assumes source-level sign symmetry under null

multiplicity.p_holm_6: six planned CORR comparisons separately per metric; includes BOTH and RF
multiplicity.existing_p_holm_21: 21 all-arm pairwise contrasts separately per metric from statistics.json; separate MC stream
multiplicity.p_holm_global_66_numeric: additional sensitivity: 6 comparisons x 11 requested numeric outcomes; excludes pattern diagnostic and unavailable human outcomes

audit.statistics_family_note: 21 valid pairs per requested numeric metric; correction_impulse diagnostic uses only 10 valid pairs (missing p omitted)

definitions.lpips: AlexNet LPIPS; preserved map weighted by area-resampled official edit-mask complement; receptive fields cross region boundary
definitions.ssim: existing background-region metric; local windows may cross mask boundary
definitions.object_mae: existing object_mae; region identity follows dataset masks
definitions.nfe: nfe_total, complete standalone cost; constants by arm, structural budget differences
definitions.joint: descriptive source-level semantic/retention quadrants and mean Pareto; no human joint-success labels available

interpretation: CORR versus ENERGY: similar semantic means; full LPIPS improves and survives global 66-test Holm; preserved LPIPS and SSIM improve under 6-comparison Holm but not 21-comparison or global 66-test Holm.

U25 descriptively dominates CORR across all five full-image semantic/retention means on 40 sources, at 91 versus 97 NFE. On the common 33 preserved-region sources CORR target CLIP is higher, so strict dominance disappears.
FLOW versus CORR has stronger directional editing and lower LPIPS/full and preserved plus higher SSIM, with 52 versus 97 NFE; CORR DINO mean is higher but uncertain.
BOTH versus CORR improves target and directional CLIP while worsening LPIPS, DINO and SSIM; semantic and LPIPS changes survive global 66-test Holm, DINO and SSIM do not.
RF versus CORR is a strong retention versus semantic tradeoff. No human joint-success measurements are available.
Pareto sets are descriptive coordinatewise comparisons, not inferential dominance or semantic equivalence; nonsignificant semantic differences do not establish equivalence.
